paper.title: The Art of Scaling Reinforcement Learning Compute for LLMs
key_claims: Proposes framework for predicting RL scaling using sigmoid curves
Conducts 400,000+ GPU-hour systematic study of RL scaling
Proposes SCALERL recipe combining multiple design choices
Shows recipe scales predictably to 100,000 GPU-hours
Claims state-of-the-art performance vs GRPO, DAPO, others
Tests on 8B dense and 17Bx16 MoE models with batch size 768

Scaling Law Validity: Method robustness to function approximation errors
Practical Considerations: Scaling law analysis ignores inference costs

weaknesses.title: Hyperparameter Fairness Unclear
weaknesses.weakness_statement: Baseline algorithms' hyperparameters are not disclosed or fairly tuned, making it impossible to assess if performance improvements are from the SCALERL method or from better hyperparameter search.
weaknesses.source_paper: MR.Q: A Model-Free Deep RL Algorithm with Model-Based Representations (R1hIXdST22)
weaknesses.source_quote: the paper provides no detail (that I could find) regarding the hyperparameter settings of the baseline algorithms, nor how or if they were tuned. This is a critical weakness of the paper, as the possibility of untuned baselines undermines the claimed performance improvements.
weaknesses.applicability_to_scalerl: SCALERL combines multiple design choices (batch size 768, KL penalty weight, reward scaling, etc.). The 400,000+ GPU-hour study claims state-of-the-art results compared to GRPO, DAPO, and other methods. Critical question: Were GRPO and DAPO hyperparameters tuned with the same compute budget and methodology as SCALERL? If baselines used default hyperparameters while SCALERL recipe was extensively tuned, improvements may reflect tuning effort rather than algorithmic superiority.
reviewer_expectation: Detailed disclosure of all baseline hyperparameters
Evidence that baselines received equal hyperparameter tuning effort
Fair comparison study where both SCALERL and baselines are tuned using same methodology
weaknesses.impact_if_not_addressed: VERY HIGH - Fundamentally undermines main claims if not resolved

weaknesses.title: Limited Evaluation Scope
weaknesses.weakness_statement: Only tested on a single task domain (mathematical reasoning with MATH dataset) limiting generalization claims across different RL domains and problem types.
weaknesses.source_paper: Process Advantage Verifiers (PAVs) for RL with LLMs (A6Y7AqlzLW)
weaknesses.source_quote: Evaluation only on mathematical reasoning tasks... All experiments on a single model family (Gemma)
weaknesses.applicability_to_scalerl: SCALERL's framework claims to apply generally to 'scaling RL for LLMs,' but evaluation is limited to math tasks with batch size 768 and max sequence length 14,336. Critical question: Does the sigmoid scaling law hold for: (1) Code generation tasks? (2) Summarization or text generation? (3) Multi-turn dialogue? (4) Tasks with longer/shorter sequences? (5) Tasks with sparse vs. dense rewards? (6) Domains with different exploration requirements?
reviewer_expectation: Evaluation on at least 3-5 diverse RL task domains beyond mathematical reasoning
Analysis of how sigmoid parameters change across task domains
Discussion of task properties that affect scaling law shape
weaknesses.impact_if_not_addressed: HIGH - Generalization claims would be questioned

weaknesses.title: Missing Comparison with Closest Baselines
weaknesses.weakness_statement: Paper compares against less relevant methods rather than the most directly comparable alternatives, making it unclear what real improvements are.
weaknesses.source_paper: Process Advantage Verifiers (PAVs) for RL with LLMs (A6Y7AqlzLW)
weaknesses.source_quote: I believe that a fair comparison would be to use PRMs since they are the closest possible baseline. The authors do prempt this by stating that PRMs have only demonstrated 1-2% improvement w.r.t. ORMs but that is in the context of best-of-N search. There are no comparisons with PRMs except for Fig 5a.
weaknesses.applicability_to_scalerl: SCALERL compares against GRPO and DAPO, but: (1) Are there other systematic empirical studies on RL scaling that should be compared against? (2) Are there other papers studying how compute budget affects reward scaling? (3) Are there other works on optimal batch size, KL penalty, or reward scaling for LLM RL? Unclear which comparisons are truly the most relevant baseline alternatives.
reviewer_expectation: Explicit justification of why GRPO/DAPO are the closest comparisons
Discussion of other scaling-focused RL methods and why they weren't compared
Analysis of SCALERL vs. other empirical scaling studies
weaknesses.impact_if_not_addressed: HIGH - Core empirical claims weakened without proper baseline comparison

weaknesses.title: Inconsistent Scaling Behavior Not Explained
weaknesses.weakness_statement: Method/framework shows benefits from certain hyperparameters inconsistently across conditions, but lacks clear intuition for why the scaling behavior varies.
weaknesses.source_quote: Increasing Synthetic Data ratio does not benefit PGR and the unconditional baseline equally. PGR scales better at r=0.75 than SYNTHER but neither benefits from 0.875. We would think the trend would be consistent? whats the intution behind this?
weaknesses.applicability_to_scalerl: SCALERL uses sigmoid curves to model scaling: reward ∝ sigmoid(compute_budget). Critical question: (1) Is the scaling monotonic across all compute budgets tested (up to 100,000 GPU-hours)? (2) Are there any non-monotonic behaviors or plateaus? (3) If scaling law parameters change with compute budget or model size, what explains these variations? (4) Why does the sigmoid model fit better than power laws or other scaling functions?
reviewer_expectation: Analysis of scaling curve consistency across different compute budget ranges
Investigation of when/why sigmoid assumptions hold vs. break down
Explanation of non-monotonic behaviors if any exist
weaknesses.impact_if_not_addressed: HIGH - Undermines predictability claims if scaling isn't monotonic

weaknesses.title: Ablation Studies Lack Statistical Rigor
weaknesses.weakness_statement: No significance testing or comprehensive analysis of which components actually contribute to performance gains vs. which are just implementation details.
weaknesses.source_paper: MR.Q: A Model-Free Deep RL Algorithm with Model-Based Representations (R1hIXdST22)
weaknesses.source_quote: The ablation study fails to provide the statistical significance of the results and lacks analysis. Furthermore, the 'reverting to theory' ablations are highly unsurprising so provide little contribution, and many of the remaining ablations show minimal performance gains.
weaknesses.applicability_to_scalerl: SCALERL recipe combines multiple design choices: (1) Batch size 768, (2) Max sequence length 14,336, (3) Specific KL penalty coefficient, (4) Reward scaling strategy, (5) Learning rate schedule, (6) Entropy coefficient. Critical question: Which components actually drive scaling improvements with statistical significance? For each component: Is the improvement > statistical noise? How does importance vary across compute budgets? Are there redundant/unnecessary components?
reviewer_expectation: Ablation study with error bars and significance tests
Analysis of contribution of each design choice to final performance
Discussion of which choices are fundamental vs. hyperparameter tuning
weaknesses.impact_if_not_addressed: HIGH - Unclear which recipe components are actually important

weaknesses.title: Critical Design Choice Justification Missing
weaknesses.weakness_statement: Paper doesn't clearly explain why specific algorithm components are necessary vs. just implementation details or task-specific tuning.
weaknesses.source_paper: Q-SFT: Q-Learning for LLMs via Supervised Fine-tuning (v4MTnPiYXY)
weaknesses.source_quote: Reuse of the pretrained weights is emphasized as the main motivation, but some of the tasks actually train the model from scratch and others are not in natural language, which is a bit conflicting.
weaknesses.applicability_to_scalerl: Critical question for each recipe component: (1) Why is batch size 768 specifically? Would 512 or 1024 work as well? Is this universally optimal or task-specific? (2) Why the specific KL penalty weight? Is this fundamental or tuned for math tasks? (3) Why these reward scaling coefficients? Do they generalize to other RL tasks? (4) Are components chosen because they're fundamentally necessary or because they happened to work best on math tasks?
reviewer_expectation: Clear explanation of which recipe components are fundamental vs. tuned
Sensitivity analysis for each hyperparameter
Discussion of how to adapt recipe to new tasks
weaknesses.impact_if_not_addressed: HIGH - Recipe applicability to other domains questioned

weaknesses.title: Scaling Law Analysis Ignores Inference Costs
weaknesses.weakness_statement: Theoretical scaling laws don't account for practical inference time costs during RL training, which may change optimal model size and scaling trajectory.
weaknesses.source_paper: Decision Transformer for Fault Detection in UTM Systems (UUwrBhhsxT)
weaknesses.source_quote: The evaluation metrics introduced by the author do not seem to take into account the cost of model inference. If it is taken into account, will the observed scaling law still hold? Or will Sweetspot be a specific model size?
weaknesses.applicability_to_scalerl: During RL training with 8B or 17Bx16 models: (1) Inference cost (forward passes to get rewards) is a significant component of total compute, (2) Larger models have higher inference costs, (3) The sigmoid scaling law may change when accounting for inference costs, (4) The optimal compute allocation might differ in practice.
reviewer_expectation: Analysis of total compute including inference costs
Discussion of how scaling law changes with inference overhead
Practical guidance on optimal model size when inference costs matter
weaknesses.impact_if_not_addressed: MEDIUM - Practical applicability of results questioned

weaknesses.title: Single Model Architecture Evaluation
weaknesses.weakness_statement: Tests only on specific model families (8B dense, 17Bx16 MoE) without exploring if scaling laws hold across different architectures.
weaknesses.source_paper: Divisive Normalization in CNNs (OovfCS4FYT) - generalized pattern
weaknesses.source_quote: Evaluation limited to outdated architectures (AlexNet, VGG-16) that are far from state-of-the-art; no scaling to modern networks
weaknesses.applicability_to_scalerl: SCALERL tests on 8B dense and 17Bx16 MoE models. Critical question: (1) Do sigmoid scaling curves hold for other architectures (e.g., vision-language models, code models)? (2) Do MoE models follow the same scaling law as dense models? (3) How do architectural differences (attention heads, layer widths, etc.) affect scaling parameters? (4) Would the recipe parameters change with different architectures?
reviewer_expectation: Evaluation on at least 2-3 additional architectural variants
Analysis of how architecture affects scaling law parameters
Discussion of architecture-specific considerations
weaknesses.impact_if_not_addressed: MEDIUM - Generalization of scaling law to other models questioned

weaknesses.title: Convergence Assumptions Violated in Practice
weaknesses.weakness_statement: Theory assumes certain convergence properties but practical experiments show violations, requiring workarounds that undermine theoretical guarantees.
weaknesses.source_quote: While the derived results are of course interesting on their own, one has to ask from a practical standpoint whether deriving & using something based on wrong assumptions makes a lot of sense
weaknesses.applicability_to_scalerl: SCALERL assumes sigmoid scaling with well-defined parameters. Critical question: (1) Are the assumptions about monotonic reward improvement with compute actually valid? (2) Are there cases where increasing compute doesn't improve reward (e.g., optimization challenges, local minima)? (3) Does the sigmoid model capture all scaling behavior or miss important phenomena? (4) What happens when assumptions are violated?
reviewer_expectation: Analysis of when sigmoid assumption holds vs. breaks down
Discussion of theoretical assumptions and their practical validity
Alternative models for cases where sigmoid fails
weaknesses.impact_if_not_addressed: MEDIUM - Theoretical foundation of scaling law questioned

weaknesses.title: Generalization Across Data Heterogeneity Unclear
weaknesses.weakness_statement: Method/framework handles homogeneous settings well but lacks analysis of how scaling behaves with diverse data sources or task structures.
weaknesses.source_quote: The data sources are not always clear given a dataset. The proposed pipeline only works if the domains are known. Otherwise, some manual or automatic clustering has to be used to create different sets of data.
weaknesses.applicability_to_scalerl: SCALERL uses math tasks with relatively uniform structure (GSM8K, MATH). Critical question: (1) How does scaling law change with diverse reward structures? (2) Do heterogeneous RL tasks (mixing multiple task types) follow the same sigmoid curve? (3) How does data distribution shift affect scaling law fit? (4) Would mixed-task training change the scaling parameters?
reviewer_expectation: Evaluation on heterogeneous task mixtures
Analysis of scaling law robustness to task diversity
Discussion of task properties affecting scaling
weaknesses.impact_if_not_addressed: MEDIUM - Robustness of scaling law to task diversity questioned

weaknesses.title: Optimal Hyperparameter Ranges Unclear
weaknesses.weakness_statement: Experiments may use suboptimal ranges for hyperparameter sweeps, potentially missing where performance actually begins to degrade significantly.
weaknesses.source_paper: Deconstructing What Makes a Good Optimizer for Autoregressive Language Models (zfeso8ceqr)
weaknesses.source_quote: For pretraining percentage and beta_2, I encourage the authors to include more extreme values to support the claim that these hyperparameters do not matter. Instead showing them they do not matter in the current small range, it is more informative to show to the readers at what extreme values the loss starts to increase significantly.
weaknesses.applicability_to_scalerl: SCALERL tests batch size 768. Critical question: (1) Is batch size 768 truly optimal or just in a tested range? (2) What happens with extreme batch sizes (1, 4096, 16384)? (3) Where do scaling curves begin to degrade? (4) Are there regime shifts in the scaling law at different compute budgets?
reviewer_expectation: Wider hyperparameter ranges tested and reported
Clear identification of regime boundaries
Analysis of scaling law beyond tested ranges
weaknesses.impact_if_not_addressed: MEDIUM - Robustness of selected hyperparameters questioned

weaknesses.title: Method Robustness to Function Approximation Errors
weaknesses.weakness_statement: Approach assumes accurate models/reward functions but doesn't validate performance when approximation breaks down at different scales.
weaknesses.source_quote: The curiosity-based relevance function relies on a learned dynamics model, which might be challenging to train accurately in complex environments.
weaknesses.applicability_to_scalerl: SCALERL uses learned reward models for training. Critical question: (1) How does reward model quality affect sigmoid scaling fit? (2) As compute increases, does reward model accuracy scale similarly or differently? (3) How robust is sigmoid fitting to reward model errors at different scales? (4) Does the scaling law hold when reward model is misspecified?
reviewer_expectation: Analysis of robustness to reward model quality
Empirical results varying reward model fidelity
Discussion of error propagation through scaling law
weaknesses.impact_if_not_addressed: MEDIUM - Practical robustness of method questioned

weaknesses.title: Presentation Clarity Issues
weaknesses.weakness_statement: Complex notation and unclear descriptions make it difficult to understand what the core contribution actually is.
weaknesses.source_quote: Overall, the paper is quite hard to read, even if you have a background in both RL and orthogonal ML. I think the notation could be improved significantly.
weaknesses.applicability_to_scalerl: The sigmoid curves and scaling parameters in SCALERL could be explained more intuitively. What do the parameters actually represent in RL terms? Why is sigmoid the right functional form? Clearer connection between compute budget and reward performance needed.
reviewer_expectation: Improved clarity of core concepts
Intuitive explanations of sigmoid scaling
Clear connection to RL principles
weaknesses.impact_if_not_addressed: LOW - Paper would be harder to read but not rejected

key_reviewer_questions: Why should we believe improvements are from SCALERL recipe and not better hyperparameter tuning of baselines?
Does the scaling law generalize beyond math tasks?
Which recipe components actually matter and have statistical significance?
Are you comparing against the most relevant baselines for scaling studies?
Does sigmoid model hold in practice or are there regime shifts?
How do inference costs affect the practical scaling law?
How sensitive are results to the batch size, KL penalty, and other hyperparameters?
Do scaling curves vary significantly across different model architectures?
Is the sigmoid model the best functional form or would power laws fit better?
How robust is the scaling law to reward model errors?

CRITICAL: Disclose all baseline hyperparameters and provide evidence of equal tuning effort
Explicitly justify why recipe components are necessary vs. just implementation details
HIGH: Evaluate on at least 3-5 additional RL task domains beyond mathematical reasoning
Add error bars and statistical significance testing to ablation studies
Explicitly justify baseline selection and compare against other scaling-focused RL methods
Analyze consistency of scaling curves across compute budget ranges
MEDIUM: Include inference costs in total compute accounting and analysis
Test on 2-3 additional architectural variants beyond 8B dense and 17Bx16 MoE
Validate sigmoid assumptions and discuss failure modes
Test on heterogeneous task mixtures and analyze robustness to task diversity
Extend hyperparameter sweeps to more extreme ranges
Analyze sensitivity to reward model quality
LOW: Improve clarity of core concepts and intuitive explanations
Better visualization of sigmoid scaling relationships
